how: We read the website of every New York City wedding photographer listed on Lazo (350 listings, 300 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: a Colorado chain with a New York landing page, elopement-package companies, and studios whose sites are mainly video. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: Have you shot at my venue, and can I see a full gallery from a wedding there, not just highlights?
How do you handle a Manhattan timeline: getting-ready in a hotel, portraits in a park that needs a permit, and traffic between the ceremony and the reception?
What is the delivery timeline, how many images, and is a second shooter or an album included or extra?

picks.name: Susan Shek Photography
picks.blurb: Susan Shek has photographed and filmed New York City weddings since 2005, plus engagements, proposals and events. The approach is no scripts and no awkward posing, with a personalized process laid out step by step on the site.

picks.name: Erica Reade Photography
picks.blurb: Erica Reade is a Brooklyn and NY City Hall wedding photographer who shoots vibrant, candid work in both digital and film. Her package page promises 700-plus edited photos in a private gallery within eight weeks. From Montreal, in New York since 2006, and a published beach photographer on the side.

picks.name: Asher Gardner Photography
picks.blurb: Asher Gardner shoots natural, romantic, timeless wedding photography on film for couples in New York City and around the globe. He studied photography in college, including developing film in a darkroom, and has been channeling that into weddings for more than a decade.

picks.name: A Day of Bliss Photography Inc.
picks.blurb: For over 18 years Wolfgang Freithof and Chiaki Sato have photographed weddings in New York City and across the globe as A Day of Bliss. They draw on a shared fashion photography background and offer full coverage with two photographers for every wedding.

picks.name: Jeanette Joy Photography
picks.blurb: Jeanette Joy is a boutique Long Island wedding and elopement photographer who takes on only 20 to 25 couples a year. Classic and candid, with over eight years of experience, serving Long Island and Westchester for couples who want to feel taken care of.

picks.name: RF Studios | Luxury Wedding Photography & Cinematography
picks.blurb: RF Studios in Amityville runs one coordinated photo and film team covering Nassau, Suffolk, NYC and destinations. They guide moments rather than manufacture them, step in with light direction for portraits, and build each collection starting from photography, film or both.

picks.name: Lisa Nicolosi Photography
picks.blurb: Lisa Nicolosi focuses on weddings, proposals, elopements and engagements, and typically photographs on the East End of Long Island: the Hamptons, North Fork, Montauk and Shelter Island. She works the whole Tri-State area and is available for worldwide travel; her father was an NYC firefighter.

picks.name: Fantasy Flash
picks.blurb: Fantasy Flash in Thornwood has photographed Westchester and Hudson Valley weddings for over 35 years in a fine art, candid style. The studio's goal, in its words, is images that echo the laughter, the stolen glances and the fleeting tears.

picks.name: Lenny & Melissa Photography
picks.blurb: Lenny and Melissa are a Woodbridge husband-and-wife team who shoot 30 weddings a year and capture real moments rather than staged poses, with handmade albums and a signature Wedding Premiere Party. They publish where their pricing starts because, as they put it, you should not have to inquire to learn the cost.

picks.name: Ben Lau | NJ Wedding Photographer
picks.blurb: Ben Lau is one half of a husband-and-wife team that owns three wedding photography brands in the NYC Tri-State area, shooting fun, candid, photo-documentary work out of Plainfield. Coverage with Ben starts at $6,200 and coverage with his team at $3,500, with ten hours of wedding-day coverage.

picks.name: Brian Delia Photography
picks.blurb: Brian Delia Photography is a Verona husband-and-wife studio that has covered thousands of weddings across New Jersey and NYC since 2009. Every wedding gets two experienced lead photographers rather than rotating associates; collections begin at $3,000, with most couples investing from $4,500.

picks.name: Diya Studios Photography
picks.blurb: Bhavin of Diya Studios grew up in Piscataway and picked up his first professional camera in 2008. His blog of simple, creative, modern NJ and NYC weddings features rooftop Indian weddings and a Jersey City celebration at Porta.
